strategy: Frontier expansion and space denial, rebuilt on F's own one-ply mechanism: for every legal action, execute a real copy of the game (game.copy().execute(action), the same call ValueFunctionPlayer.decide() makes) and score the RESULTING state with catanatron.players.value.base_fn(DEFAULT_WEIGHTS) -- the exact function/weights F runs. B03's identity (denial) is an additive bonus on top, scaled below base_fn's production weight (1e8) so it only breaks near-ties base_fn already found close: a contest premium when the targeted settlement node or road's far node lies in the opponent's real board-graph reach (2 hops, computed from STATIC_GRAPH + current road/building state, never a snake-order or Manhattan-coordinate assumption), plus a small steal bonus on MOVE_ROBBER when a victim is available.
config: weights inline in agent.py (CONTEST_BONUS=3.0e6, STEAL_BONUS=1.0e6); no external dependencies beyond the supplied engine
human_builder: Avadooth (implemented and tested with coding-assistant review in this session)

runtime_contract.fallback: first ROLL, else first END_TURN, else index 0; wrapper never raises to the harness

calibration_history: first cut used CONTEST_BONUS=2.5e7 (reasoned as 'well below the 1e8 production weight'); screen result 21/80 (26.25%), WORSE than v001's 29/80 (36.25%)

diagnosed: typical production deltas between candidate sites are themselves ~1e7-4e7 (pips 0.1-0.4 times 1e8), so 2.5e7 was overriding genuine production differences rather than only breaking near-ties
rescaled to CONTEST_BONUS=3.0e6 (~1/10 of a typical production delta); rerun screen-b03v2-vs-f-02: 39/80 (48.75%)
known_weaknesses: still below 50% in the final head-to-head vs B04 v002 was exactly even (20/40); vs F it is close but not proven superior at this sample size (seat-paired 0.4875 +/- 0.2147, 95% Hoeffding)
no sampling of hidden dev worlds (unlike F's own epsilon/search variants); single real-state 1-ply lookahead only
contest bonus magnitude was tuned by one recalibration pass against one 40-board screen, not cross-validated against a held-out board set

CPU rose from v001's ~0.02s/game mean to ~0.44s/game mean (game.copy()+execute() per candidate action, same mechanism F itself uses) -- still comfortably inside the per-game budget (up to 1.5s) but worth monitoring if the action-list fans out wider on other maps
